Strategy Kill embedded runtime / corresponding source

Upstream: https://github.com/libnoname/noname
Revision: 2367607e246d21aae168dba15c01151ee0651f30 (v1.11.6)
Code license: GPL-3.0-only. Preserve LICENSE and UPSTREAM-README.md;
the latter contains additional non-commercial language whose release impact
must be reviewed by the release owner. Local integration is not legal clearance.
No upstream artwork, fonts, voices or sound recordings are included.

Contents
- upstream-source.tar.gz: pinned readable upstream source and build inputs.
- source-manifest.json: source paths and upstream Git blob/SHA256 provenance.
- adapter-source/: modified bootstrap, read-only filesystem and product mapping.
- vendor/fake-indexeddb-6.2.4/: readable ESM source, with its Apache-2.0 license.
- licenses/: notices for bundled runtime dependencies.
- poc-integrity.json: exact inventory of the original reviewed browser build.
- assemble.py: deterministic source/notice packaging and delivery manifest.

Building the upstream core
Extract upstream-source.tar.gz to a working directory. With Node.js 24 and
pnpm, install the supplied workspace using its lockfile (pnpm install
--frozen-lockfile), then run pnpm --filter noname build. The upstream build
entry is apps/core/scripts/build.ts. Do not run the upstream dev file server
in the product. It is not part of the read-only integration.

Adaptation
Use apps/core/dist as build output. In noname/init/import.js, directly after
async function importFunction(type, path) {, add:
  path = new URL('../../' + path.replace(/^\//, ''), import.meta.url).href;
Copy the four adapter-source files to the runtime root. Copy the readable
fake-indexeddb 6.2.4 ESM files to vendor/fake-indexeddb-6.2.4. The bootstrap
replaces browser persistence with memory-only storage before loading noname.
Only members listed by poc-integrity.json are imported; omit host.html and
host.js. The original static-files.json is read-only engine lookup metadata,
not an HTTP allowlist. Original artwork/audio and unlisted modes are excluded.
A fresh upstream rebuild requires review and a newly approved inventory;
assemble.py deliberately refuses changed upstream bytes instead of approving
them automatically. It is not a byte-reproducible upstream build claim.

Product assembly
The repository's buildStrategySetup('H01') is the authority for
adapter-source/approved-setup.json. The selected player may vary per game;
the child validates all 31 character records against this approved mapping.
In the runtime repository run python vendor/strategy-kill/assemble.py.
It copies approved adapters, packages source.tar.gz and notices, then writes
manifest.json containing version=1, entry=sandbox.html, path/byteLength/sha256.
The two product Vite builds emit those exact bytes. The server exposes only
manifest members via the restricted strategy-runtime namespace, with an opaque
allow-scripts iframe, runtime-only CSP and no credentialed CORS or API bypass.

Verification
pnpm exec tsx --test tests/strategy-runtime-assets.test.ts tests/strategy-runtime-package.test.ts
pnpm --filter @agent-v/cloud-server build:knowledge-card
pnpm exec tsx --test server/test/strategy-runtime.test.ts server/test/strategy-kill.browser.test.ts
The product browser tests exercise actual UI and the upstream engine. Native
AI termination is not replaced by a fabricated finished message or game.over.

Local 0.1.1 adapter verification (2026-10-06)
Upstream runtime inventory and character mapping are unchanged. The adapter
reserves native table lanes, keeps a bounded 200-row public log view, corrects
compact equipment contrast, labels own equipment outside engine-owned equips,
and adds a separate keyboard-accessible current-public-skill help dialog.
Boot pause ownership includes host desiredPaused, visibility and native help;
the configure/pause/resume message whitelist and opaque sandbox are unchanged.
Run npm test and npm run test:pack -- /absolute/artifacts/path.
Set STRATEGY_BROWSER_TOOLS to an existing package.json resolving playwright-core
and run npm run test:native -- /absolute/evidence/path (existing Edge on Windows).
Tests use the approved engine and synthetic public fixtures, never private user
inputs or forced termination. This is a local package, not a public release.
